title: Service-level load gate: the operations, the file columns, the effect list, the parameter rows and the SCR-42 panel split are not named for rwb-access
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3.md (RWB-AD-015 Endpoints, Data, Screen and states, Permission checks); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (T-A.2 API-P4-005 and API-P4-006); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (A2.17, Screens); _work/msr/context/P4.md (ownership rows)
section: 1 Story; 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.2; 14; 15 Screens and states
description: RWB-AD-015 asks for the time allowed in each case state, its warning point and its escalation point loaded as data, approved, with the effect on timers. Five values behind that request have no source. (1) The operations: the legacy Endpoints table names only the general rule-version pair /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-versions and /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-versions/{versionId}/approve, TSD P4 v3 declares the general reference-load pair API-P4-005 and API-P4-006 with the rights Reference data C and A, the P4 ownership rows carry only GET /admin/access-log, GET /admin/roles, GET /me/session and POST /admin/break-glass-grants, and no source names the access-side service-level load, its approval path or its read. (2) The service-level file: no source gives the column names, their order, the delimiter, the header row or the size and row limits of the file. (3) The effect on a running timer and the version label: the legacy criterion says a running timer keeps its due date unless the rule says to recompute, but no source gives the fields of that effect per timer, the possible outcomes or the label of a stored version. (4) The parameter rows carrying the four-eyes switch and the row and file limits, and the reference list codes of the state set and the working-day calendar, are unnamed. (5) The SCR-42 panel split: the P4 ownership rows give rwb-access no queue operation and no screen, so which service serves the queue panel and which serves the service-level panel is not stated. The story proposes the three operations on the access base, reads the file columns and the effect list from the case service's contract, reads parameters and reference data through DP-06 and DP-07, and leaves the split to the gateway-bff composite route; each choice is an assumption.
evidence: RWB-AD-015 Endpoints (POST /admin/rule-versions/{versionId}/approve, POST /admin/rule-versions), Screen and states (SCR-42 Queues and service levels: Versions, load; SCR-39 Rules and parameters: Versions, load, approval) and Test cases TC-AD-015-01 to TC-AD-015-04; TSD P4 v3 T-A.2 API-P4-005 (POST /admin/reference-loads, multipart file, table, validFrom) and API-P4-006 (POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve); FSD P4 A2.17.3 and the Screens table (SCR-42, SCR-39); context pack P4 'REST operations provided (4)' and 'Events (0)' with no service-level operation.
owner_role: Solution architect, P4 and the P3 owner of the service-level and timer contract
proposed: Confirm the three access-side paths, the file columns and the effect fields at the wave 4 contract review with the P3 owner of RWB-P3-E1028-CON, name the parameter rows and the reference list codes with the parameter catalog owner, and agree the SCR-42 panel split with the gateway-bff owner.

title: The right letters of the service-level load and approval differ between the legacy story and TSD P4 v3
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3.md (RWB-AD-015 Permission checks); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (T-A.1 and T-A.2, API-P4-005 and API-P4-006)
description: The legacy story's permission table gives the load of a service level to Rules and parameters C, held by RW-COE, and the approval to Rules and parameters A, held by RW-RISK. TSD P4 v3 declares the same two-step load of timers inside the reference-load pair with the rights Reference data C for API-P4-005 and Reference data A for API-P4-006, and the legacy delegation story RWB-AD-016 lists Reference data C as held by RW-COE and RW-REFADM. The two sources therefore disagree on the capability area whose letter opens the load and the approval, and no source says whether the access-side gate uses the reference-data letters or the rules-and-parameters letters. The story applies the legacy permission table, because it is the story's own statement of who may load and who may approve, and it records the disagreement for the contract review.
evidence: RWB-AD-015 Permission checks ('Rules and parameters | A | RW-RISK', 'Rules and parameters | C | RW-COE'); TSD P4 v3 API-P4-005 ('Authorization | Reference data, right C, scope applied') and API-P4-006 ('Authorization | Reference data, right A, scope applied'); RWB-AD-016 Permission checks ('Reference data | C | RW-COE, RW-REFADM').
owner_role: Solution architect, security administrator role, P4
proposed: Decide at the wave 4 contract review whether the service-level gate keeps the legacy Rules and parameters letters or moves to the Reference data letters of the reference-load inventory, and state the decision once in the contract document so the app story and the SCR-42 console apply the same letter.

title: The contract document of the access-side service-level load has no declared source for its paths, schemas and error bodies
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench API Specification v4.yaml (/admin/reference-loads, /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (T-A.2); _work/msr/context/P4.md
description: The contract slice publishes an OpenAPI 3.1 document for the three access-side operations, but no declared source fixes its content. The API Specification v4 declares the monolith paths /admin/reference-loads and /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve with the schemas ReferenceLoad and a multipart request of file, table and validFrom, and it declares neither a read of a load nor a separate service-level resource; TSD P4 v3 adds no schema beyond the operation names. The document therefore has to declare ServiceLevelLoad, ServiceLevelRow and RunningTimerEffect, the state set of a load, the error bodies of the 422 and the 409, and the consumed operations of rwb-case, and no source gives the property names, the state names or the body shapes. The story fixes these as the baseline and marks each one as an assumption, so the app story and the P3 owner build against a named artefact rather than a guess.
evidence: API Specification v4 /admin/reference-loads (summary 'Load reference data: lists, queues, timers, templates, delegation limits') and /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve; TSD P4 v3 API-P4-005 and API-P4-006 (request mp file, table, validFrom; response ReferenceLoad; errors 401, 403, 409, 422, 503); context pack P4 (REST base /api/recovery/access/v1, schema rwb_access, topic rwb.access.events.v1).
owner_role: Tech lead, P4 and the API specification owner
proposed: Publish the baseline and have the P3 owner of RWB-P3-E1028-CON and the API specification owner agree the three schemas, the state set and the 422 and 409 bodies at the wave 4 contract review, then freeze them as the fake pack of 12.8.
